reviews.review: My first Extraction shooter game, I find it hard but very fun to play and it’s better if you play with friends

TL;DR: The TealDeer here is pretty simple: Game's got good bones, with decent gunplay, an interesting world, and interesting map design. However, the playerbase seems divided and toxic, and as player numbers drop, the experience becomes far less pleasant for those who prefer a PvE-focused adventure. Devs will do what they feel is best or right, but with a significant cheater and duping problem alongside the vitriol being spread through the game, at least from where I sit, I cannot recommend anyone spend money on this game unless they're very specifically here for a PVP-focused game.

The Body:

Before I say anything else, let me say that I DO enjoy the game's general premise, the world they have set up, MOST of the gameplay I've experienced, and so on. This isn't intended to be a hate-fest or anything, just an honest review with my opinion and enough backstory to explain that opinion. I've held off on reviewing this game at all for a fairly long while now, for a few reasons. For one, I was able to rack up around seventy-ish hours in the game, and for most of that, I had a pretty decent time. Ran peaceful, so I rarely had to deal with being killed. (I hear the screaming already...) The ARC were a pretty decent threat, and I was starting to get a fair number of BPs that would let me deal with the bigger ARC enemies, take part in the whole Queens and Matriarchs stuff. I was pretty excited for it, not gonna lie. The problems started around sixty-five-ish hours in, for me anyway. Despite my play style remaining the same, PVP opponents became more and more common in my lobbies. Rats became even more common. Still, I toughed through it, got better at staying hidden while I looted. Mostly just needed basic materials for crafting supplies, anyway, and I ran a pretty basic kit that anyone could get from a slightly-lucky free-loadout spawn.

Around that sixty-five-ish hour mark, it was as if someone had flipped a switch. Out of, I don't know, twenty or thirty raids during those last few hours, I was hit by PVP in all but, at most, a half-dozen. Many were no-comms PVPers, whom I can respect well enough, I get their jam even if I don't enjoy it. The ones that drove me off were the ones who responded to my 'Woah, easy, peaceful!' calls with derision and insults. I'm not here to say that the PVP playerbase is toxic- like with any community in a game like this, both sides of the apparent divide in this game, PVP and PVE, have their share of toxic a$sholes- but I WILL say that from my point of view, the number of toxic PVP players spiked basically overnight, between one gaming session and the next. Many, MANY of those toxic players were rats who set up their little ambush near to the extract points. 

After around ten or twelve hours of getting hammered pretty hard by PVP players, I decided that whatever had changed, the game was no longer for me. I shrugged and moved on, because no game is permanent. Only became aware of just how nasty the community discourse had become when a random youtube Gaming News channel mentioned 'the Arc Raiders Community Controversy' in passing while discussing Marathon and Destiny. I got curious, and peeked into the steam community tab for the game. First: Wow. It's... It's full of vitriol, from both sides of the disagreement. Second: Apparently, there is a very, very rampant duping and cheating issue in the game, based on the things I've read in the community. So I decided I'd keep up with it a little bit, started checking in every few days. Fast forward a few weeks, and I believe I've gathered enough information on the current state of things to be confident enough on my opinion to share it in this review, summarized by whether I recommend the game. Cheating, duping, and an overly-caustic interaction between players who generally run PVE and those who generally run PVP has created a very mixed experience for the game. Bans seem to catch players uninvolved in cheating, in some cases those who haven't played in months, creates additional friction points, and a general lack of content has led to an increase in PvP player numbers and a decrease in PvE players.

In my opinion, the Extraction Shooter genre is both very niche and is currently oversaturated, and there's always a split between those players who want to experience the world without the friction of actual PvP, and those who find the PvP to be a main selling point. Most games, notably Escape from Tarkov, another game I have a lot more experience with, offer a PvE-only option in order to broaden the appeal of the game itself, allowing a live service game such as this to continue to gain funding via those PvE-focused players. There's a great deal of disagreement about that in the game's community, which is fair. My opinion on this is that all games die eventually, but I believe that this game's death will come about sooner if something isn't done to satisfy those who, like me, were driven off by the PvP friction. If their goal is a ten-year game, as I've seen floated in the community, then a PvE mode is a must, not because it would fix anything in particular, but because it would broaden the appeal and allow them to make more money from the game over time. However, I also believe in the idea that the free market allows devs to create whatever they want, and people are able to decide whether to buy it and support it. The devs will do what they think is best or right, and I am behind their choice in that 100%.

I'm just one of the number who won't be one of their active players if there's no environment that allows me to be my peaceful, robot-killing PvE-focused self. Should they add in a PvE mode, I personally feel that it would solve enough of the persistent problems I've read about or witnessed myself that I could justify recommending the game. Until then... Sorry. I can't recommend playing it.
